name: Alila Ubud
positioning: Hillside jungle resort above the Ayung River near Ubud, blending contemporary design with traditional Balinese architecture
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet jungle retreat with valley views
Guests interested in Balinese culture, wellness and village experiences

facts.text: Alila Ubud sits on a hillside above the Ayung River, surrounded by jungle canopy.
The resort blends contemporary design with traditional Balinese architecture.
The rooms and villas overlook the Ayung River Valley and are designed to resemble a Balinese village.
Lower-floor rooms have individual garden terraces, and high-floor rooms have spacious balconies with jungle views.
Deluxe rooms have a private garden terrace and back courtyard, an outdoor bathtub and shower, and garden and valley views.
The Pool Villa has a private pool and an open-air tub among lotus, and includes in-villa check-in and check-out.
The Two Bedroom Villa is the resort's largest, with a private pool, outdoor tubs and a separate dining area.
Spa Alila combines contemporary wellness products and services with ancient Asian healing techniques.
A weekly wellness program includes sunrise yoga, Qi Gong and Tai Chi.
Guests can craft their own silver piece side by side with local Balinese artisans, or work alongside a farmer in the rice fields.
Plantation Restaurant serves Asian specialties in a Balinese wantilan-style pavilion with an alang-alang roof, overlooking the Ayung River valley.

highlights.text: The Terrace Tree Villa is a treehouse-like retreat atop the valley, with a terrace looking over the rainforest canopy.
The Valley Villa has valley views, an outdoor tub in a lotus pond and alang-alang roofing.
The resort has an infinity pool set among lush greenery.
On the Journey Through Purification and Prayer, a Balinese high priest pours blessed water over guests during the Melukat blessing.
Spa Alila offers the lulur body scrub, an ancient village remedy that originates from Bali rice farmers.

considerations.text: The resort sits outside Ubud town rather than in its center; travel time depends on traffic.
The resort is about 40 kilometers from I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport.
WhataHotel notes limited nightlife and dining options in the immediate vicinity.
